concepts.title: Who Is a Citizen
concepts.definition: A citizen is a full member of the political community - bound to the country by law and allegiance, enjoying civil, political and social rights, and owing duties in return; citizenship links individual freedom with shared responsibility for the nation.
concepts.key_idea: Citizenship is a two-way bond: rights flow to the citizen, duties flow back to the community.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees205.txt lines 5-62 (rights and duties, meaning of citizenship)
question_patterns: who is a citizen of India
what does citizenship mean beyond legal status
how is a citizen different from an alien
what rights and duties come with citizenship
how can citizenship of India be acquired
why is citizenship called a relationship of mutual obligation

solution_steps.explain: Citizenship grants full civil and political membership of the state.
Rights to equality, freedom, vote and protection belong to citizens.
Obedience to law, civic sense and service balance the rights.

concepts.title: Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution
concepts.definition: The Constitution guarantees fundamental rights - equality, freedom, against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and constitutional remedies - protected by courts, so no government or person may trample them.
concepts.key_idea: Six families of fundamental rights, enforceable in court, shield every citizen.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees205.txt lines 153-227 (fundamental rights in the Indian Constitution), 421-460 (key articles)
question_patterns: name the fundamental rights given by the Indian Constitution
which article provides equality before law
how can a citizen enforce fundamental rights
why are fundamental rights called fundamental
what does the right against exploitation prohibit
explain the right to constitutional remedies with an example

solution_steps.explain: Recall the six groups from equality to constitutional remedies.
They bind the state and, in some cases, private persons too.
Writ jurisdiction of courts makes these rights enforceable.

concepts.title: Duties: The True Source of Rights
concepts.definition: As the chapter's epigraph says, the true source of rights is duty: fundamental duties - respecting the constitution and flag, protecting the environment, striving for excellence and renouncing practices derogatory to women - are what citizens owe so that everyone's rights can flourish.
concepts.key_idea: Rights and duties are two sides of one coin - my duty secures your right.
question_patterns: list the fundamental duties of Indian citizens
how are rights and duties related
why are duties called the true source of rights
what duty do citizens owe to the environment
explain the duty to strive towards excellence
give two examples where performing a duty protects others' rights

solution_steps.explain: Every right implies a matching duty in others and in oneself.
Respect for law and symbols, environment protection, harmony and excellence head the list.
A citizen demanding rights must first perform the duties that sustain them.

concepts.title: Equality and the Fight Against Discrimination
concepts.definition: Discrimination - unfair treatment on grounds of caste, religion, gender or birth - violates the constitutional promise of equality; abolishing untouchability and reserving opportunities for the disadvantaged are constitutional tools to convert formal equality into real equality.
concepts.key_idea: The constitution not only bans unfair treatment but actively lifts the historically excluded.
question_patterns: what is discrimination - define with an example
how does the constitution fight caste discrimination
what is untouchability and what does the constitution say about it
how do reservations promote equality
distinguish formal and substantive equality
suggest ways students can fight discrimination in school

solution_steps.explain: Treating people unequally by birth or belief is discrimination.
Abolition of untouchability, equality clauses and reservations attack it.
Equal behaviour in daily life completes legal equality.
